blocks.content: Metrics Server is the lightweight, in-cluster component that actually collects the CPU and memory metrics HPA, and kubectl top, depend on, without it installed, autoscaling based on resource usage simply cannot function.
1. Collecting Basic Metrics From Every Node
blocks.text: 1. Collecting Basic Metrics From Every Node

blocks.content: Metrics Server continuously collects basic CPU and memory usage data from every kubelet in the cluster, covered in the Architecture module, aggregating it into a simple, queryable API.

blocks.alt: A continuous, lightweight collection pipeline, pulling data straight from every node

blocks.content: This is exactly where the data behind the HPA topic actually comes from, when an HPA watches CPU utilization, it is reading directly from Metrics Server, without it running, there is simply no data for the HPA to make decisions from at all.

blocks.alt: The literal data source behind every CPU or memory-based HPA decision

blocks.content: The familiar kubectl top nodes and kubectl top pods commands, covered in the kubectl module, read from this exact same Metrics Server, not some separate, dedicated monitoring pipeline.

blocks.alt: The same data source, also powering a command you likely already use

blocks.content:
kubectl top pods
# NAME      CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
# my-app-1  120m         256Mi

code.content:
kubectl top pods
# NAME      CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
# my-app-1  120m         256Mi

codes.bash:
kubectl top pods
# NAME      CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
# my-app-1  120m         256Mi

blocks.content: 4. Deliberately Lightweight, Not a Monitoring Solution
blocks.text: 4. Deliberately Lightweight, Not a Monitoring Solution

blocks.content: It is worth being precise about scope: Metrics Server provides only current, real-time resource usage, it stores no history, and it is not a substitute for a real monitoring stack like Prometheus (covered in the Monitoring & Logging category), for dashboards, alerting, or historical trends, you need that instead.

blocks.alt: Real-time only, deliberately lightweight, not a replacement for real monitoring

blocks.content: This is worth knowing before ever configuring an HPA, without Metrics Server actually installed and running in the cluster, an HPA based on CPU or memory simply has no data to act on, it is a genuine, easy-to-overlook prerequisite.

blocks.alt: A real, easy-to-miss prerequisite worth checking before an HPA is expected to work

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Metrics Server collects real-time CPU and memory data from every node, the literal data source behind HPA decisions and kubectl top.
It is deliberately lightweight, with no history, not a substitute for a real monitoring stack like Prometheus, and it is a genuine prerequisite HPA cannot function without.
